entities.name: Query RNase E/G protein
observations: 768 aa protein with predicted molecular mass of 86.6 kDa and theoretical pI 6.49.
Pfam S1 RNA-binding domain spans residues 36–117.
Pfam RNase_E_G domain spans residues 121–391 with very strong support (i-Evalue 2.7e-101).
Pfam RNase_E_G_Thio domain spans residues 403–488 with strong support (i-Evalue 6.5e-32).
C-terminal half is enriched in Lys/Arg, acidic clusters, proline-rich low-complexity segments, and repeated basic motifs, consistent with regulatory or RNA/protein-interaction regions.
Sequence homologs include P21513 at 90.7% identity over 77.7% of the query and additional homologs at 74.6–79.1% identity.
Protein-search annotation transfer was not automatically accepted; functional assignment is therefore based mainly on domain architecture and homology evidence.
No transmembrane segment or N-terminal secretion signal is evident from the sequence architecture; a soluble intracellular localization is favored.

entities.name: RNase E/G endoribonuclease
observations: Members contain an N-terminal catalytic RNase E/G region often associated with an S1 RNA-binding module and participate in bacterial RNA maturation and degradation.
The query sequence architecture is consistent with an RNase E/G-family endoribonuclease, but exact substrate specificity and organism-specific functions are not established from this analysis alone.

entities.name: Bacterial RNA turnover
observations: The predicted RNase E/G catalytic domains support possible roles in endoribonucleolytic processing and degradation of cellular RNA, including transcript maturation and RNA decay.
This process assignment is family-level inference rather than a directly retrieved curated annotation for the query sequence.
